senses.sense_definition: To swarm over, spread throughout, or occupy in large numbers, often causing harm or damage.

examples.text: If you do not weed the garden regularly, wild plants will soon <w>overrun</w> the entire yard.
The abandoned building was completely <w>overrun</w> with weeds and insects.

senses.sense_definition: To exceed the planned time limit or schedule.

examples.text: Because the opening speech began late, the entire meeting was forced to <w>overrun</w> the schedule.
The morning presentation will likely <w>overrun</w> by fifteen minutes.

senses.sense_definition: To defeat and invade a territory or enemy position quickly and completely.

examples.text: The military forces managed to <w>overrun</w> the enemy stronghold after hours of intense fighting.
Enemy soldiers threatened to <w>overrun</w> the border defenses.

senses.sense_definition: To run past or extend beyond a intended stopping point or boundary.

examples.text: The distracted runner failed to stop in time and <w>overran</w> the finish line.
The aircraft <w>overran</w> the runway due to icy landing conditions.

senses.sense_definition: To exceed a specified financial budget or limit.

examples.text: If the project managers do not control expenses carefully, costs will <w>overrun</w> the budget.
The construction project threatens to <w>overrun</w> the original estimate.

senses.sense_definition: To carry text or type over into the next line, column, or page.

examples.text: The editor adjusted the font size so that the paragraph would not <w>overrun</w> onto the next page.
Long titles often <w>overrun</w> into the second line of the layout.

senses.sense_definition: To oppress, trample upon, or treat harshly.

examples.text: The aggressive rulers sought to <w>overrun</w> the weaker populations of the region.
No ruthless conqueror shall be allowed to <w>overrun</w> the rights of the citizens.

traits.comment: used in historical or literary contexts

senses.sense_definition: An instance of exceeding a budget, time limit, or estimated cost.

examples.text: Poor planning and unexpected delays resulted in a major cost <w>overrun</w> for the new highway project.
The company suffered a severe cost <w>overrun</w> during the development phase.

senses.sense_definition: The specific amount or extent by which something exceeds a limit.

examples.text: The financial team calculated a significant <w>overrun</w> at the end of the quarter.
Management worked hard to reduce the financial <w>overrun</w> before the audit.

senses.sense_definition: A designated, clear area beyond the end of a runway designed to allow an aircraft to stop safely if it fails to halt in time.

examples.text: The pilot used the paved <w>overrun</w> to bring the aircraft to a safe complete stop.
Engineers extended the runway <w>overrun</w> to improve safety standards at the airport.

senses.sense_definition: The percentage of air incorporated into a frozen dessert, such as ice cream, during manufacturing.

examples.text: High-quality ice cream typically has a low <w>overrun</w>, making it denser and richer.
Cheaper frozen desserts often contain too much <w>overrun</w>, giving them a fluffy texture.
